overview: Bahrain is a small island country in the Persian Gulf, linked to Saudi Arabia by a long causeway. Its capital and largest city is Manama. Bahrain became independent from British protection in 1971 and is a kingdom. Oil was found there in 1932, one of the first finds in the Gulf, and today banking and finance are also important.

geography.text: Bahrain is made up of a main island and dozens of smaller ones. The land is low and mostly desert, and parts of the coast have been extended with land reclaimed from the sea. Freshwater springs, both on land and under the sea, once made it an important stop for ships and pearl divers.

history.text: Bahrain was the centre of the ancient Dilmun civilisation, a trading hub between Mesopotamia and the Indus Valley. It was ruled by Portugal and Persia before the Al Khalifa family took control in 1783. Bahrain became a British protectorate in the 1800s, found oil in 1932, and became independent in 1971.
